title: Software Engineer, Infrastructure Security
desc: About the Team Security is at the foundation of OpenAI's mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Security team protects OpenAI's technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but operational in how we execute, and we support every product and research effort at OpenAI. Our tenets include prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers and developers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and fostering a strong, collaborative security culture. About the Role OpenAI is seeking a Security Software Engineer to join the Infrastructure Security (InfraSec) team. InfraSec safeguards the core of OpenAI's research and production environments—GPU supercomputing clusters, multi-cloud infrastructure, datacenters, networking, storage, and the critical services that power our frontier AI models. Our charter spans everything from bare-metal hardware and firmware to Kubernetes clusters, service meshes, and the data pathways that carry highly sensitive model weights and user data. As a Security Software Engineer, you will design and build critical foundational services, such as authentication systems, egress/ingress proxies, access brokers, and key management platforms, that demand high standards of reliability, scalability, and software craftsmanship. These systems form the security backbone of OpenAI's supercomputing environment and must remain robust under intense scale and adversarial pressure. In this role, you will: - Architect and implement production-grade security services (e.g., auth services, access brokers, secure proxies, key-management infrastructure) that provide strong guarantees across hardware, operating systems, Kubernetes, networks, and CI/CD. - Partner with infrastructure and research engineers to embed security into high-performance compute clusters, enabling rapid model training and deployment without compromising protection. - Develop automation and detection tooling to continuously identify and mitigate risks in large-scale cloud and on-prem environments. - Drive high-impact initiatives such as line-speed encryption, machine identity, and network isolation, continuously raising the security bar for emerging AI workloads. - Lead or participate in design reviews and threat models to ensure new systems launch with strong security foundations and operational excellence. You will thrive in this role if you have: - Strong software engineering skills in languages such as Python, Go, Rust, or C/C++, with a track record of shipping and operating high-reliability distributed services. - Experience building or operating critical security infrastructure (e.g., auth services, service-to-service proxies, certificate or key-management systems). - Deep understanding of security principles, best practices, and common vulnerabilities. - Expertise in securing large-scale cloud platforms (e.g., Azure, AWS, GCP), including multi-cloud networks and cloud-agnostic system design. - Familiarity with container and orchestration security (Kubernetes, service meshes) and modern authentication/authorization standards (OIDC, mTLS, SPIFFE/SPIRE). - A proactive mindset, with the ability to identify and address security gaps or inefficiencies through automation and tooling. - A track record of delivering scalable solutions and driving impactful changes across infrastructure in real-world projects. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with an ability to think critically and objectively assess security risks. - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to convey complex security concepts to technical and non-technical stakeholders. - Excitement about collaborating with cross-functional teams to build secure, reliable systems that scale globally. Our goal is to revamp this to a new, more flexible experience by building systems that leverage AI/LLMs to gain a deeper understanding of the types of jobs pros want and can do. This new system will learn and improve as pros use it, rather than remaining static, ultimately helping pros secure more and better jobs. We've built conviction through research, experiments, and market-based tests that doing this successfully would be a big unlock for Thumbtack. We are starting to pilot this with a small group of pros. Joining this team now means you are joining an area that already has high conviction and momentum behind, but still has plenty of opportunity to be involved in driving the strategy and making large product changes. Successfully achieving this will not only strengthen Thumbtack's partnership with our pros but also unlock greater impact on the marketplace side and enhance the overall customer experience. ## The challenge The primary challenge for an Engineering Manager (EM) within the New Hiring Experience org that the Pro Feedback and Targeting team is part of is to help homeowners across the U.S. search for and hire the most relevant home service professionals—and ultimately get their jobs done. We address this by tackling complex problems at the intersection of engineering, data science, and applied science. We help homeowners start more projects on Thumbtack by enabling them to express their needs in everyday, conversational language through our search bar. This involves solving underlying challenges around query comprehension and problem scoping. As customers define their project, we help them share their preferences and availability to better match them with the most relevant professionals. We then support them in comparing and selecting the right pros for their job. ## About the Role We are seeking an Engineering Manager for one of the cross-functional product teams (pods) within the larger New Hiring Experience org. Drive execution against team goals and OKRs while guiding the team through complex technical tradeoffs and delivering high-quality outcomes. - Hire, coach, and manage full-stack engineers at all levels, including Staff+ engineers, while developing future technical leaders through regular feedback, performance management, and career development. - Build and evolve a high-performing culture of excellence, accountability, and continuous learning on the team. - Be accountable for maintaining, scaling, and operating the infrastructure owned by your team. - Work closely with other engineering leaders to evolve Thumbtack's engineering culture, strengthen organizational effectiveness, and improve engineering practices in a high-paced growth environment. ## In order to be successful, you must bring - You will play a critical role in helping families make one of the most important decisions of their lives. Your ability to follow through, guide effectively, and drive outcomes directly impacts both family experiences and business success. desc: A Place for Mom is building the future of senior care, and design is central to how families, caregivers, providers, and APFM teams navigate that experience. We are looking for a Staff Product Designer to own product design for Consumer Experience and help us turn emotionally complex care decisions into clear, trustworthy, high-quality product experiences. APFM is organizing around the two customers that define our marketplace: families navigating care decisions and providers delivering care. Evolving toward a more connected experience across the full care placement journey. This role is for someone who is curious about where product design is going, not only where it has been. We do not expect anyone to have ten years of experience with tools that are only beginning to emerge. We do expect you to be actively experimenting with AI tools, learning where they help, where they fail, and how they can create leverage without replacing judgment, craft, accessibility, ethics, or deep user understanding. You will partner with Product, Engineering, Research, Marketing, Analytics, Operations, Sales, and business leaders to shape consumer journeys that help families understand their options, build confidence, and take the next best step in a high-stakes senior care decision. Who you are: You are a high-agency builder: someone who moves toward ambiguity, takes ownership without waiting for perfect direction, and uses design, data, and AI-native tools to make the team move faster and raise the quality of the work. You care about users, business outcomes, product quality, and team momentum. You have strong design judgment, but you are not precious about process. You know when to prototype, when to simplify, when to push for a better system pattern, and when to help the team make a pragmatic decision. You are AI-forward without being AI-naive. You are curious about tools like Figma Make, Figma Agents, Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, MCP-enabled workflows, v0, or similar tools, and you have probably tried some of them before they were fully ready. You understand that these tools can accelerate exploration, synthesis, prototyping, and production, but that they also introduce limitations, quality risks, trust concerns, and new responsibilities for designers. You bring strong interaction design, information architecture, systems thinking, and product judgment to complicated consumer decision journeys. You can work across acquisition, education, search, intake, matching, comparison, and conversion experiences without losing sight of the broader marketplace and service journey. What you will do: Lead design for Consumer Experience - Own end-to-end product design for Consumer workstreams, from discovery and journey mapping through prototypes and production-ready design, including the unified family experience across APFM.com, AgingCare, Care Hub, advisor-connected workflows, and emerging AI-enabled channels. - Translate emotionally complex, information-heavy senior care decisions into intuitive workflows that help families move forward with confidence. - Partner with Product, Engineering, Research, Marketing, Analytics, Operations, Sales, and business leaders to define problem framing, success criteria, tradeoffs, and release scope. - Design for trust, clarity, accessibility, speed, and usability across moments where families need accurate information and confident next steps. Shape product direction with evidence - Use research, analytics, care-seeker conversations, marketing insights, funnel data, frontline team input, product data, and business context to guide design decisions. - Identify high-leverage opportunities where better consumer experiences can improve family outcomes, provider outcomes, and business performance. - Communicate design rationale clearly to product teams, engineering partners, marketing partners, operational stakeholders, and senior leaders. - Help teams understand not only what should ship, but why it matters. Raise the design quality bar - Apply and extend shared APFM patterns so consumer product surfaces feel coherent across channels and touchpoints. - Help distinguish consumer-specific design needs from reusable marketplace and design-system patterns. - Contribute to shared foundations, including interaction patterns, information architecture, accessibility, UX writing, content quality, and craft standards. - Mentor and raise the bar for other designers through critique, pattern quality, and strong product storytelling, without requiring people-management responsibility. Increase design leverage with AI - Bring a builder's mindset to design: use lightweight prototypes, AI-assisted workflows, and scrappy experiments to make ideas tangible earlier. - Experiment with AI tools to explore product directions, prototype consumer journeys, synthesize inputs, pressure-test assumptions, and improve the speed and quality of design work. - Help the team understand where AI meaningfully improves the consumer experience, and where human judgment, trust, accessibility, and clarity matter more. - Share what you are learning with Product, Engineering, Research, Marketing, Analytics, Operations, Sales, and design partners so the team gets better together. Qualifications: - 7+ years of product design experience on complex consumer web, marketplace, healthcare, search, lead-generation, ecommerce, SaaS, CRM, internal-tool, or operations-facing products. - Strong portfolio showing end-to-end ownership from ambiguous problem framing through shipped product, including work that influenced product strategy or raised the quality bar across multiple workstreams. - Excellent interaction design, systems thinking, information architecture, UX writing judgment, and product judgment. - Demonstrated curiosity and hands-on experimentation with AI tools in the design or product development process. - Ability to explain not just what you designed, but how you used evidence, tools, prototypes, constraints, and judgment to make better decisions. - Experience working in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where ownership, pragmatism, and cross-functional trust matter. - Strong Figma skills and the ability to communicate design intent through flows, prototypes, specs, and crisp design storytelling. - Comfort partnering deeply with Product Managers, Engineers, Researchers, Marketing, Analytics, operational stakeholders, Sales, and senior leaders to align teams around clear design direction. title: Staff Product Manager, Acquisition & Growth
desc: ## About the Role We are looking for a Staff Product Manager to own how families discover, trust, and choose A Place for Mom across organic search, AI-mediated discovery, and emerging surfaces, and to build the product-led growth systems that turn discovery into qualified, high-intent demand. You will design and ship the product systems that drive sustained organic acquisition in a category where trust, authority, and decision quality are everything. You will partner across Product, Engineering, Data, Marketing, and Brand, and own measurable acquisition outcomes. This is a product role with deep SEO expertise required, not an SEO role with product seasoning. If you have spent your career shipping product surfaces that move organic acquisition, with a strong SEO foundation and a working point of view on how the search landscape is evolving, this is for you. ## What You'll Own Organic acquisition - Own the product strategy and roadmap for how APFM's owned properties perform across the traditional, AI-mediated, voice, and agentic search landscape - Translate SEO signals, algorithm shifts, and discovery changes into product decisions and roadmap prioritization; partner with specialist practitioners who own day-to-day execution AI / Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and emerging distribution - Define and evolve how A Place for Mom shows up across the full AI-mediated discovery landscape, including AI search citations, conversational query coverage, structured data for AI grounding, MCP integrations, voice interfaces, and agentic endpoints - Monitor and interpret shifts in AI platform behavior, search landscape changes, and evolving distribution surfaces, and translate them into internal product guidance, guardrails, and prioritization - Evolve existing AI discovery measurement framework and tooling as the ecosystem develops and new channels come online that require new measurement approaches Product-led growth - Build acquisition loops into the product surface: Sharing, comparison tools, decision aids, community-driven content surfaces - Partner with Product peers to embed PLG mechanics in core flows that compound organic acquisition without paid spend Measurement and opportunity sizing - Define metrics, baselines, and targets for organic and AI discovery; size opportunities, set hypotheses, and lead learning agendas - Translate ambiguous, evolving discovery signals into actionable product bets and clear investment recommendations Trust and authority (YMYL) - Senior care is a Your Money Your Life category; embed authority, expertise, and trust signals into product surfaces and content systems - Ensure the signals AI systems use to evaluate credibility, including review integrity, content quality, and decision support depth, are reflected accurately in what we build - Develop and maintain a point of view on AI disintermediation risk and ensure the product roadmap accounts for it ## What Success Looks Like in 12 Months - APFM's leadership position in AI search citation share is maintained and extended into new surfaces and query types as the landscape evolves - Organic acquisition growth in high-intent segments is accelerating, with a clear product roadmap driving continued improvement - At least one new distribution surface, such as an MCP integration, voice endpoint, or agentic integration, is live and attributable - The AI discovery measurement framework has evolved to account for new channels and surfaces that didn't have measurement approaches when you arrived - Trust and authority signals are meaningfully strengthened in the product surface, with a clear and defensible point of view on how APFM wins in an AI-mediated world - At least one product-led growth loop is live inside a core flow and compounding organic acquisition without paid spend ## What You Bring - 7–10+ years of experience in SEO, organic growth, product strategy, or related roles - Demonstrated depth in SEO fundamentals and a track record of shipping product surfaces that moved organic acquisition outcomes, not just advising on them - A working point of view on how the search landscape is evolving: how AI-mediated discovery works, how to instrument and influence it, and where it's heading - Comfort with ambiguous, evolving data sets and the ability to build measurement approaches where none exist yet - Strong opinions on trust-sensitive, YMYL content and product systems - Proven ability to write clear requirements, run experiments, partner closely with engineering, and own delivery end-to-end - Experience facilitating alignment across senior stakeholders in ambiguous, cross-domain problem spaces - Experience managing or mentoring other practitioners; a track record of elevating the product intuition and execution quality of the team around you - Bonus: marketplace or aggregator experience, regulated or health-adjacent domains, prior GEO work, MCP or agentic distribution experience ## Why You'll Love It Here - High-leverage influence across multiple products and cross-functional partners - The chance to define how SEO, generative engine optimization, and product-led growth evolve together ## Compensation - Our team owns the agency portal where senior living and home care providers manage referrals and their relationship with A Place for Mom. This position reports to the Senior Engineering Manager – B2B Platform. You will work across the full stack: React/TypeScript experiences in Grace, .NET services behind our unified API layer, and Python ingestion pipelines that pull provider data from NPPES, state licensing boards, and other sources into Databricks. You will help select the technologies, architectural patterns, and design approaches the team adopts, and provide technical direction to a team of engineers building the systems our partners depend on every day. We expect this engineer to work with LLMs as a first-class part of the job. That means using agentic coding tools fluently to move faster, and building LLMs into the product where it creates real leverage - data extraction and normalization at scale, entity resolution, classification, and workflow automation. Candidates who treat LLMs as an afterthought will not be a fit for this role. Who you are: The ideal candidate is a hands-on, outcome-oriented engineer who is comfortable owning a problem from the database to the browser. You have extensive experience as a strategic technical leader. You have designed, built,, and supported production systems. title: Territory Partner (Field Sales)
desc: ## The Role Omada AI is the AI marketing platform built for small businesses — and we grow the old-fashioned way: in person, face to face, business by business. Territory Partners are the front line of that motion. This is a true field sales role. You'll walk into local businesses, pitch owners directly, and get them live on Omada the same day. You find your own prospects, build your own pipeline, and close your own deals. There's no cold-call center behind you and no calendar of pre-booked meetings waiting when you log in — the TPs who win here are the ones who don't need one. If you've done outside sales before and you know the feeling of turning an empty morning into three signed customers by dinner, keep reading. ## What You'll Do - Prospect your territory relentlessly. Identify, approach, and pitch local SMBs — walk-ins, door pulls, referrals, local networking, whatever works. You own your pipeline end to end. - Sell in person. Pitch business owners face to face and get them started in a live free trial on the spot — we don't do demos or demo accounts. You build their system on their real business, with their real content, in front of them. - Run the full sales cycle. From first conversation through trial activation to paid conversion, the deal is yours. - Master the product fast. Omada is straightforward to learn and pitch — most reps are confidently selling within their first day or two. The hard part isn't the product; it's the hustle. That's why we hire for the hustle. - Report and improve daily. Track your activity, present your accounts in team reviews, and sharpen your close rate week over week. ## How We Set You Up to Win - Two-week apprenticeship. You start paired with a veteran Territory Partner: shadow their pitches, then prospect together, then close your own deals with their help (with commission split during the ramp). No classroom fluff — you learn this job by doing this job next to someone who's great at it. - Proving Ground. Our performance-gated ramp structure rewards producers quickly. Hit your numbers and your earnings and territory opportunities grow with you. - A real career ladder. TP → Vanguard → City Captain → State Director → Regional Director → Country Manager. We promote from the field, full stop. - A product that sells. SMB owners need marketing help, most can't afford an agency, and Omada does the work of one for a fraction of the price. When you get in front of the right owner, this sells. ## Who We're Looking For Required: - Proven field / outside sales experience — you've sold face to face before (D2D, B2B field, territory sales, retail energy/telecom/payments, or similar) and you have the numbers to show for it - Demonstrated self-prospecting ability — you've built your own pipeline from zero and you're comfortable walking into a business cold - Closer's mentality — you ask for the business, handle objections in the moment, and don't leave without a next step - Self-managed and disciplined — you run your day like a business owner, because as a 1099 contractor, you are one - Reliable transportation and the ability to work your territory in person daily You'll thrive here if: - You'd rather be paid for what you produce than for showing up - You like small business owners and can talk to a plumber, a salon owner, and a realtor in the same afternoon - You're energized (not intimidated) by rejection volume - You want a shot at building and leading a market, not just working one This is not for you if: - You're looking for a role where meetings are booked for you - You need warm leads handed over to get going - You've only sold over the phone or by email and aren't sure about face-to-face ## Compensation Commission-based with performance-gated ramp compensation through our Proving Ground structure. Top producers earn well above typical field sales roles — your income is a direct function of your production. Full details shared during the interview process. ## About Omada AI Omada AI is a Seattle-headquartered AI marketing platform for small businesses, backed by HubSpot Ventures and Crosslink Capital. We're growing fast across the US and promoting our field leaders as we go. Ready to own a territory? Apply now — our hiring process moves quickly, including a short async video interview and a conversation with a field leader in your region.

Partner with data engineering to maintain and evolve the automated pipelines that generate daily prospect scores, distribute scored prospects to the sales floor, and replicate scoring data into downstream CRM and sales systems. - Present analytical findings and strategic recommendations directly to sales executives and operations leaders, translating model outputs and data into clear narratives that drive decisions on rep headcount, prospect mix, and outreach strategy. - desc: Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading. About the role: Backend engineering rarely gets this consequential. As a Senior Software Engineer on Camunda's Core / API & Process Automation team, you'll work on the beating heart of Camunda 8 — the event-sourced, distributed workflow engine that executes business-critical processes for thousands of customers and, through them, millions of people worldwide. Because you sit at the core, one well-made improvement propagates outward through every integration and product built on top of it: a small change here is felt everywhere. Few systems demand this. You'll squeeze the last drops of performance out of the hot paths. You'll design maintainability and versioning strategies for an engine that must faithfully replay every event it has ever written — forever. You'll reason about the concurrency between the engine advancing a process and a user mutating that same process in the same instant. And you'll hold an unforgiving bar: data must never be corrupted, and a process must never get stuck — because when it does, customers lose money. That single constraint cascades into some of the hardest technical and product challenges you'll find anywhere. You'll also help define what comes next. Enabling AI agents to integrate with and drive the engine is cutting-edge work, and the features we ship create real aha moments and stretch what the industry thinks automation can do. You'll do it alongside a world-spanning team of highly skilled, highly motivated engineers who share one goal: make Camunda the best workflow engine in the world. As a senior here you set the technical bar — you take ambiguous problems and give them shape, lead the hard discussions, and make the people around you better. Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we're solving complex problems at scale What You'll Be Doing: - Design, build, and evolve the event-sourced engine and its C8 REST/gRPC/MCP API (command/event, CQRS), including safe public-API evolution — backward-compatible changes, versioning/deprecation, and contract tests so existing integrations and AI agents never break. - Take on hard, ambiguous problems and lead them end-to-end — define the problem, write the solution design (ADR), weigh trade-offs pragmatically, sequence the work, and drive delivery across the team. - Ship high-impact engine features fast — such as suspending and resuming individual process instances, and enabling AI agents to steer running processes — all while simplifying the engine and holding it to an extremely high quality bar. - Ship resiliency, schema evolution, and observability — smooth version upgrades, replay safety, migration correctness on the event log, and features diagnosable in production, not after the fact. - Detect and optimize inefficient processing and data-access patterns across our data stores (RocksDB, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, relational/Postgres) — spot shapes that don't scale, and fix them. - Level up the team and lead incidents — high-quality reviews, mentoring, and winning technical debates with reasoning (a role model who cares deeply about product and team, not a lone hero); on call, drive resolution, own the RCA, and feed systemic fixes back into the platform. What You Bring: - Ability and/or willingness to use our product - 5+ years professional backend engineering, with real depth in distributed and event-driven systems. - Deep event sourcing / distributed execution knowledge— consistency, ordering, replay, and their failure modes (partitions, crashes, duplicate/reordered delivery, idempotency, recovery). - Strong API design and evolution — contract-first, backward-compatible change, versioning/deprecation, contract testing. - Diagnosing/fixing performance under production load — profiling, benchmarking, tail-latency and backpressure reasoning. - Technical leadership from ambiguity — work autonomously, break down undefined problems, drive pragmatic decisions, disagree-and-commit, and level other engineers up (not a lone hero). - Communication & product sense — crisp technical writing (ADRs that decide things async), remote-first collaboration, deep product thinking, and an outstanding manager of one. Nice-to-haves: - Experience with workflow automation / process orchestration (BPMN or similar). - Awareness of the consensus/replication protocols the engine builds on (Raft, SWIM, etc.) — enough to design the engine to behave correctly on top of them (this layer itself is owned by another team). - Deep query-pattern optimization in RocksDB, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch and relational/Postgres. - Solid JVM knowledge (memory model, concurrency/perf). title: Staff Software Engineer (AI Governance)
desc: We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to help shape AI governance for developer tooling at Coder. This role sits on our AI Governance team, which builds and maintains two enterprise-grade components of Coder's AI governance stack. AI Gateway is a centralized LLM gateway that sits between coding agents and providers such as OpenAI or Anthropic, providing organizations with audit trails, token tracking, cost control, and centralized authentication. Agent Firewall wraps those agents with default-deny network policies, controlling which domains and methods they can reach inside workspaces. title: Clinical Operations Liaison (Full-Time, Remote)
desc: ## ABOUT US At Sprinter Health, our mission is to dramatically expand access to healthcare by reimagining the patient experience—delivered at home and powered by technology for scale. We're building the technology and clinical services platform to make preventive, connected healthcare accessible for everyone in the US. We deliver hybrid care (in-home + virtual) backed by data products across 15+ states, serving 60%+ of the US population through major health plans and systems. With 1M+ patients and 92+ NPS, we're rapidly scaling our impact. Our team of technologists, clinicians, and operators is backed by investors including a16z, General Catalyst, GV, and Accel. We have a rapidly growing team of visionary leaders who are passionate about increasing access to care, lowering healthcare costs, and improving outcomes for patients. ## ABOUT THE ROLE We are growing rapidly and are looking for a Clinical Operations Liaison to support our clinical leaders as we scale our field operations and clinical teams. You'll be the connective thread between our NPs and Sprinters (our clinician field staff) and the operational systems that keep them paid, trained, and compliant — handling workforce tracking, payroll compliance follow-up, documentation review, and reporting so clinical leadership can stay focused on patient care, clinical support, and clinical oversight. We're not just looking for someone to execute a checklist. As we scale, we want someone who notices where a workflow is clunky, a tracker is out of date, or a process could run smoother — and speaks up about it. You'll have real opportunities to help shape how these processes evolve. This is a remote full-time position. This role reports to the Director of Quality & Training. ## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES ## Workforce & Payroll Compliance - Serve as the day-to-day point of contact for NPs and Sprinters on timesheet, mileage, and documentation questions - Follow up with field employees on timesheet submissions, PTO entries and approval, and sick time to ensure accuracy before each payroll close - Validate weekly mileage and hours are submitted in accordance with policy and protocols - Review and abstract supporting documentation for mileage and time submissions - Approve expenses within set parameters - Data pulls and tracking for peer audits, bonus incentives - Deliver a weekly exception report to each manager — escalations only, with full documentation - Other duties as assigned ## Workforce Operations & Reporting - Maintain clinical employee attendance, call-off, and workforce planning trackers - Track training completion in Sprinter University and annual compliance for clinical teams - Prepare weekly and monthly operational reports for your assigned clinical area - Support logistical planning for workforce - Maintain dashboards, trackers, and workforce metrics - Other duties as assigned ## Escalation & Program Support - Manage administrative escalation trackers and ensure timely follow-up on open items - Route non-clinical operational issues to appropriate teams - Maintain SOPs, workflows, and operational documentation - Track project milestones and action items; support new workflow launches as directed by the In-Home Director ## Compliance & Quality - Participate in internal audits; identify documentation gaps and recommend process improvements - Flag recurring issues or inefficiencies in existing workflows and propose fixes to your manager - Maintain confidentiality and adhere to all HIPAA and compliance standards ## YOU'LL LOVE THIS JOB IF - You take pride in accuracy and integrity, finding satisfaction in getting every detail right - You're motivated by mission as much as metrics — knowing your work directly supports better access to preventive and chronic care for patients nationwide - You thrive in a tech-forward, fast-growing environment where innovation and continuous improvement are part of the daily rhythm - You enjoy working independently in a remote setting while staying connected to a collaborative, purpose-driven team - You're naturally curious, proactive, and eager to contribute feedback and shape evolving processes - Most of all, you value flexibility, accountability, and being part of a company that's reimagining how healthcare reaches people where they are ## ABOUT YOU You will thrive at Sprinter Health if you have: - A desire to work collaboratively with a tight-knit but quickly growing team across many different areas of the business - Flexibility, humility, and a sense of humor - Excitement for working in a fast-paced, high-growth environment Experience and Skills: - 2+ years in an operations, coordination, or administrative support role - Experience managing multiple workflows, trackers, or reports simultaneously - Comfortable working independently and remotely with minimal day-to-day direction - Strong communication and problem-solving skills - Proficient in EHR systems and Google tools - Reliable internet connection and dedicated, secure workspace - Available to work CST hours Preferred: - Experience in healthcare operations, medical group administration, or home health/home care - Familiarity with multi-state payroll or leave compliance - Experience supporting a distributed or regional field team - Prior use of Rippling or a similar HRIS platform ## THIS ROLE DOES NOT INCLUDE - Disciplinary action or performance management - Clinical, patient-facing, or care coordination responsibilities ## TECHNOLOGIES WE USE - Slack - Google Suite (Docs, Slides, Sheets) - Rippling or similar HRIS platform The compensation range for this position is $65,000–$75,000 annualized + benefits. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Sprinter Health is an equal opportunity employer and encourages all applicants from every background and life experience to apply.

title: Clinical Support Nurse, RN (Temporary)
desc: About Us Sprinter Health is an on-demand mobile health service that sends medical professionals to patients' homes to perform blood draws, diagnostic and low acuity services, and wellness visits. We are building the clinical and technological infrastructure to realize a future of healthcare untethered. We have a rapidly growing team of visionary leaders who are passionate about increasing access to care, lowering healthcare costs, and improving outcomes for patients. About The Role The Interim Clinical Support Nurse provides real-time support for Sprinters and the clinical team, including clinical escalations, patient safety events, and abnormal laboratory result management. This role partners closely with Patient Operations, Clinical Operations, Quality, Product, and other cross-functional teams to improve workflows, drive operational excellence, and ensure timely, safe, and high-quality patient care. The ideal candidate is an experienced nurse leader with strengths in people leadership, clinical decision-making, project management, quality improvement, and process development. ## Key Responsibilities Clinical Operations - Provide operational oversight for clinical escalations, patient safety concerns, and abnormal and critical laboratory result workflows. - Ensure timely resolution of clinical issues while meeting service level agreements (SLAs). - Provide clinical guidance and operational support to Sprinters and the clinical team for complex clinical questions, patient safety concerns, and escalations. - Manage staffing, workload distribution, and daily operations for Clinical RNs Quality & Patient Safety - Lead patient safety and quality improvement initiatives. - Investigate patient safety events and participate in root cause analyses and corrective action planning. - Identify trends and implement sustainable process improvements. - Ensure compliance with clinical policies, regulatory requirements, and organizational standards. - Promote a culture of quality, safety, and continuous improvement. Performance & Operations - Own monthly operational KPIs, dashboards, and service level metrics. - Analyze performance trends and identify opportunities to improve quality, efficiency, and patient outcomes. - Develop action plans to improve performance and operational consistency. Project Management - Lead cross-functional operational and clinical projects. - Develop, implement, and maintain clinical policies, SOPs, workflows, and standardized guidance. - Support implementation of new clinical programs, pilots, and operational initiatives. - Drive change management and adoption of new workflows across teams. Cross-Functional Collaboration - Partner closely with Patient Operations, Patient Support, and Clinical Operations - Identify opportunities to improve patient experience and operational efficiency. - Communicate operational updates and clinical recommendations across teams. - Support strategic organizational initiatives and process improvement efforts. ## Qualifications Required - Active, unrestricted Registered Nurse (RN) license. - Minimum three years of leadership experience. - Strong clinical judgment and decision-making skills. - Experience managing clinical escalations, abnormal laboratory result workflows, and patient safety events. - Experience leading remote initiatives - Demonstrated project management and process improvement experience. - Experience developing clinical policies, procedures, and workflows. - Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills. - Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Preferred - Compact RN license strongly preferred. - Eastern Time Zone (EST/EDT) preferred. - Experience leading a remote clinical support, nurse triage, telehealth, or centralized call center team. - Experience in healthcare quality, patient safety, regulatory compliance, and risk management. - Experience managing monthly KPIs, dashboards, and operational reporting. - Experience partnering with Patient Operations, Clinical Operations, Product, Engineering, and Quality teams. - Experience using Slack and other virtual collaboration tools. - Experience in a startup or high-growth healthcare environment. - Lean, Six Sigma, or other quality improvement experience preferred. ## Success in This Role The successful candidate will: - Deliver timely, high-quality clinical support to Sprinters and the clinical team. - Improve quality, patient safety, and operational performance. - Develop scalable clinical workflows and policies. - Build strong partnerships across Clinical Operations and Patient Operations. - Use data and KPIs to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence. This position will perform additional duties and special projects as assigned to support evolving business and operational needs.

title: Logistics Coordinator - Temporary
desc: ## Role Summary Sprinter Health is seeking a temporary Logistics Coordinator to provide after-hours and weekend coverage for our travel operations. This role will serve as the primary point of contact for time-sensitive travel and logistics needs that arise outside of standard business hours. The ideal candidate is highly responsive, organized, calm under pressure, and comfortable making decisions independently using established processes and escalation pathways. ## Key Responsibilities - Monitor designated communication channels during assigned after-hours and weekend shifts and respond promptly to urgent travel and logistics needs - Support Sprinters with time-sensitive travel issues, including flight disruptions, hotel concerns, transportation changes, and other unexpected travel needs - Coordinate and make necessary changes to existing travel arrangements using established company guidelines - Troubleshoot issues and identify practical solutions that minimize operational disruption and unnecessary travel costs - Determine when an issue can be resolved independently versus when it requires escalation - Escalate urgent or high-impact issues to the appropriate on-call team member or leader - Communicate clearly and professionally with Sprinters and internal stakeholders throughout issue resolution - Maintain accurate documentation of issues, decisions, travel changes, and associated costs - Provide clear handoffs to the weekday Logistics team for unresolved issues or items requiring follow-up - Follow established travel policies, SOPs, and escalation procedures ## Typical Issues You May Support - Flight delays, cancellations, or missed connections - Last-minute hotel changes or accommodation issues - Rental car or ground transportation problems - Unexpected changes to a Sprinter's travel assignment - Urgent travel booking or rebooking needs - Questions from traveling Sprinters requiring immediate assistance - Situations requiring escalation due to cost, safety, or operational impact ## What We're Looking For - Strong organizational skills and attention to detail - Excellent written and verbal communication - Ability to remain calm and solutions-oriented when handling time-sensitive issues - Strong judgment and ability to independently triage requests - High level of reliability and responsiveness during scheduled coverage - Comfort working independently with limited real-time supervision - Ability to follow established policies while using good judgment when unexpected situations arise - title: AI Product Designer
desc: ## Consequential Work. Dedicated People. ## About Onebrief Onebrief builds collaboration and AI-powered workflow software for military planning and operational coordination. Military planning is complex by nature, requiring teams to coordinate information, people, and decisions across systems and locations. Onebrief brings planning, collaboration, simulation, and AI into one connected environment, helping teams test strategies, adapt to changing conditions, and make decisions with greater clarity when the stakes are real. We are a distributed team of builders from military, operational, and technology backgrounds who care deeply about improving how important work gets done. Some team members work remotely, while others work directly alongside customers in operational environments around the world. Founded in 2019, Onebrief is backed by leading investors including General Catalyst, Battery Ventures, Insight Partners, Sapphire Ventures, and Human Capital. Valued at more than $2 billion, we continue to invest in product innovation, AI capabilities, and team growth. ## Why This Role Exists We're hiring a Senior AI Product Designer who can independently own the user experience for a product area and contribute quickly. This role is built for someone who can ramp fast and start shipping without heavy onboarding. You'll own the definition of what users need and how they interact with Onebrief: partnering with Product to translate essential user goals into the interface elements and behavior that support them, and making the quality-vs-speed trade-offs that keep releases moving. You'll be the one who articulates those trade-offs clearly enough, and presents solutions confidently enough, to move the team forward. You'll also build deep expertise in how our users actually work, particularly military planners operating under real-world constraints, and contribute to the design language that keeps Onebrief cohesive across surfaces. AI is one of the tools in your kit, used fluently alongside traditional design foundations, but this role is defined by the outcomes you drive: clarity for users, cohesion across the product, and trade-offs made well. ## What You'll Do - Own the UX definition for a product area: what users need, how they interact with the product, and why, partnering with Product to translate essential user goals into interface elements and behavior. - Act as the arbiter of quality vs. speed for your scope, flexing your craft to fit release priorities, and articulate trade-offs clearly enough to move teams forward. - Build deep expertise in how your users actually work by meeting with them, mapping their workflows, and documenting the human and organizational context that shapes their work so others can build on it. - Own pattern decisions for your area and contribute to Onebrief's broader design language and system, applying informed taste and craft. - Evaluate emerging AI UX patterns and apply them deliberately. Know when a pattern fits a given use case and when it doesn't. - Combine traditional design foundations and AI-native workflows to produce work across a range of fidelities, flexing between moving fast and diving deep. - Document design intent through both visual representation and written documentation for human collaborators and agentic tools alike. ## Minimum Qualifications - Track record independently owning the UX definition for a product area or workflow, end-to-end, from understanding user needs through shipped interface decisions. - Craft demonstrates expertise in foundational UX/UI concepts and practices, with concrete examples of articulating trade-offs (quality vs. speed, scope vs. fidelity) that moved a team forward. - Experience building deep user/workflow expertise firsthand through direct user research and workflow mapping, and documenting it in a way others could act on. - Has led strategic and tactical implementation of at least one major AI-based workflow in a SaaS application. - Demonstrates knowledge of emerging AI UX patterns and a clear process for evaluating when, where, and how to apply them for a given use case. - Advanced user of AI design tools, with intermediate-level knowledge of how foundational models work and their tradeoffs, not just how to prompt them. ## Preferred Qualifications - Experience contributing to or codifying design system/pattern decisions beyond your own project, helping scale consistency across surfaces. - Solid grasp of accessibility and interaction design fundamentals, with experience communicating that expertise to others. - Active, contributing member of the design systems community. - Track record of actively advancing your team's overall workflows or ability to produce effectively with AI tools and practices, not just your own individual output. ## Indicators of Success A successful Senior AI Product Designer will, within six months: - Be independently owning UX definition and trade-off decisions for their product area, with minimal oversight. - Have shipped work that used AI meaningfully in the process, not as decoration, but as a real accelerant to quality or speed. - Have documented user/workflow expertise that other designers or collaborators have actually used to make decisions. - Have contributed to or expanded Onebrief's design language in a way that improved cohesion across surfaces. - Be a trusted partner to Product and Engineering, presenting solutions and trade-offs that move projects forward. In the absence of an executed Recruitment Services Agreement, there will be no obligation to any referral compensation or recruiter fee. In the event a recruiter or agency submits a resume or candidate without an agreement Onebrief explicitly reserves the right to pursue and hire those candidate(s) without any financial obligation to the recruiter or agency. Any unsolicited resumes, including those submitted to hiring managers, shall be deemed the property of Onebrief.

We're hiring a Corporate Systems Security Engineer to help build and operate the technical security foundations that protect our corporate environment. This is a hands-on security engineering role focused on owning and improving security across endpoints, identity, SaaS applications, browsers, Zero Trust infrastructure, and the broader corporate security stack. You'll work at the intersection of security engineering, systems configuration, and automation—turning security requirements into technical controls that are measurable, repeatable, and difficult to drift away from. A major focus of this role is reducing manual security operations. Rather than repeatedly collecting the same evidence or discovering configuration drift during an audit, we want to build systems that continuously enforce our security expectations and produce trustworthy evidence of their effectiveness. You'll work closely with Corporate IT, Security Operations, GRC, and application owners, but your mandate is security: understanding how systems can be abused or misconfigured, establishing secure defaults, and ensuring the controls protecting Onebrief continue to operate as intended. ## What You'll Do You'll help own and mature the security systems protecting Onebrief's corporate environment. Core responsibilities include: - Own and improve enterprise security technologies across areas such as EDR, SIEM, MDM, Zero Trust, identity, browsers, and SaaS applications, including deployment, configuration, integrations, monitoring, and lifecycle management. - Establish and enforce secure configuration baselines across corporate systems, continuously identifying configuration drift and building durable mechanisms to remediate it. - Build API-driven, infrastructure-as-code, or workflow-based automation that connects security systems, eliminates repetitive security work, and makes control enforcement and evidence collection more reliable. - Partner with Corporate IT and application owners to securely deploy and operate endpoints, applications, and SaaS platforms while maintaining appropriate security boundaries and technical controls. - Improve security telemetry by integrating corporate systems and applications with centralized monitoring and ensuring the signals necessary to detect vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and suspicious activity are available and actionable. - Translate security and compliance requirements—including CMMC 2.0 and NIST-aligned controls—into practical technical implementations that can be continuously validated and supported with defensible evidence. ## Minimum Qualifications - 4+ years of hands-on experience in security engineering, enterprise security, systems security, or a closely related technical role. - Experience securing identity, SaaS, or Zero Trust environments and understanding how configuration decisions affect enterprise security. - Experience building security automation using APIs, workflow automation platforms, infrastructure-as-code, scripting, or configuration-management technologies. - Experience deploying, administering, or owning endpoint security and detection technologies such as EDR and SIEM platforms, including integrating security telemetry into centralized monitoring. - Experience administering MDM or endpoint-management platforms to enforce security configurations, and maintain endpoint baselines. - Ability to evaluate technical requirements through a security lens, identify risk in proposed configurations, and work across technical teams to implement practical controls without losing sight of the security objective. ## Preferred Qualifications - Experience owning or administering technologies such as CrowdStrike, Zscaler, enterprise MDM, identity providers, SIEM platforms, or comparable enterprise security systems. - Experience implementing technical controls aligned with CMMC 2.0, NIST 800-53, CIS/STIGs, or similar security frameworks. - Experience building integrations between SaaS or security platforms using REST APIs, webhooks, or automation platforms such as Github Actions or Okta Workflows. - Experience securing corporate environments in regulated, government, defense, or other high-assurance organizations. ## Indicators of Success This role will evolve as priorities change, but the outcomes below reflect what success typically looks like in the first six months. A successful Corporate Systems Security Engineer will: - Become a trusted technical owner for key components of Onebrief's corporate security stack, with clear understanding of their architecture, configuration, integrations, and security posture. - Reduce configuration drift across corporate endpoints, SaaS applications, identity systems, and security tooling through measurable baselines and automated enforcement. - Improve the reliability and coverage of security telemetry by integrating critical corporate systems with centralized monitoring and addressing meaningful visibility gaps. - Replace recurring manual security and compliance processes with automation that improves control consistency and produces reliable, reusable evidence. - Identify and remediate systemic security weaknesses rather than treating individual findings as isolated configuration issues. - Improve Onebrief's ability to demonstrate that corporate security controls are continuously operating as intended, reducing the effort required to prepare for audits and assessments. ## Tools, Systems & Technologies The specific technology stack will continue to evolve. Relevant areas include: Endpoint & Detection: EDR (crowdstrike), vulnerability management, SIEM (splunk), endpoint telemetry Device Management: MDM (Workspace One), application deployment, configuration profiles, endpoint baselines Identity & Access: Identity providers (Okta), SSO, MFA, lifecycle management, conditional access Network & Zero Trust: Zero Trust access platforms (Zscaler), secure web gateways, browser security, network security controls SaaS Security: Enterprise SaaS administration, configuration management, logging, access controls, API integrations Automation: REST APIs, webhooks, no-code/low-code security automation, infrastructure-as-code, configuration management Security & Compliance: CMMC 2.0, NIST 800-53, security baselines, continuous control validation, audit evidence Notice to Third Party Recruitment Agencies Please note that Onebrief does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or employment agencies. You understand the full software development lifecycle (design, review, testing, release) and you know where reliability fits into each step. You're comfortable reading and writing application code, and you're just as happy dropping into a kubectl shell to triage a production issue. You turn failure modes into guardrails, and you think monitoring, alerting, and clear runbooks are part of building software, not extra credit. You mentor others and push a culture of blameless postmortems. desc: ## Consequential Work. Dedicated People. ## About Onebrief Onebrief builds collaboration and AI-powered workflow software for military planning and operational coordination. At Onebrief, you will own the models and data that make those answers defensible in AtomEngine, our cloud-based simulation engine for military planning. You will lead the technical standards and production workflows behind AtomEngine's entity catalog: how military platforms and capabilities are represented, which sources and formulas support their performance, and how that work is tested. Your judgment will shape the catalog that scenarios run on and the methods other analysts use to build it. As a Staff-level individual contributor, you will set standards and mentor other analysts. You will stay hands-on with research, modeling, and validation while directing AI agents to scale first-pass research, data entry, documentation, and testing. You will define tooling and test requirements with Engineering and partner on implementation. Production software development is not the primary focus. ## What you will own - Modeling standards. Research and select credible sources. Adopt, adapt, or develop defensible formulas for weapon and sensor effects, fuel consumption, survivability, and other performance characteristics. Document assumptions, uncertainty, and the conditions under which a model can be trusted. - Catalog priorities. Maintain a roadmap across service branches, nations, and eras. Work with Customer Relations to prioritize the catalog segments customers need most, and track coverage, freshness, and confidence so the team knows what to build or improve next. - AI-directed production. Design the instructions, review checkpoints, and quality controls that analysts and AI agents use to create entities at scale. Review their work, correct errors, and turn successful methods into repeatable workflows. Define requirements for tools that improve production. - Validation and testing. Lead verification, validation, and accreditation (VV&A) across catalog segments. Use source evidence and subject matter expert (SME) review to assess model credibility; partner with Engineering on continuous automated tests. Run competitive wargames with colleagues to expose gaps, challenge assumptions, and guide corrections. - Technical judgment with customers. Build a network of SMEs and resolve contested modeling decisions with customers and internal teams. Explain the evidence behind the numbers, make limitations clear, and use feedback to improve the catalog. - Shared working practices. Author standards and knowledge articles that others can apply consistently. Train and mentor analysts in research methods, modeling judgment, AI workflows, and VV&A so the catalog can grow without depending on one person's expertise. ## What you bring Experience applying modeling and simulation, systems engineering, operations research, or test and evaluation to complex systems. You can assess whether a model is credible for its intended use and explain why. Quantitative judgment: you can evaluate performance formulas, identify weak assumptions, and decide when to use an existing approach or develop a new one. You can make defensible calls when evidence is incomplete or conflicting. Ownership of complex technical work. You can translate competing needs into priorities, establish repeatable processes, and keep a large body of work organized, current, and traceable. Practical experience directing AI agents through research or analytical tasks, including clear instructions, review checkpoints, and error correction. You can evaluate their output against source evidence. Clear technical communication and the confidence to work through disagreements with customers and SMEs. You can turn your reasoning into standards and documentation others can follow. An investigative approach to simulation and wargaming: you actively look for where a model breaks and use what you learn to improve it. ## Additional experience we value AFSIM or other military simulation environments, simulation authoring, or game modding. Military doctrine, force structure, or platform performance. Test automation, QA tooling, version control, or issue tracking. Mentoring or establishing technical standards across a team. ## What success looks like Customer priorities translate into a clear catalog roadmap. Entities have traceable sources, documented assumptions, and evidence of validation. Analysts and AI agents follow repeatable production and review methods. Tests and wargames surface weaknesses that lead to corrections. Customers can understand both the basis and the limits of the models they use. Experience building production/release infrastructure such as automated pipelines, intake/evaluation systems, QA automation, or telemetry. - Familiarity with deployment processes and stacks such as Docker, EKS (Kubernetes on AWS), and GitHub CI/CD pipelines, or comparable. - Informed opinions on where and how human gates should exist versus where automation is most effective, with the ability to defend that judgment with examples. - Track record leading ambiguous, cross-functional exploratory or moonshot projects, pulling in whoever's needed regardless of role boundaries and turning exploration into something real. - Comfortable being the first and only person in a role, building the playbook rather than inheriting one. ## Preferred Qualifications - Active, contributing member of the design systems community (writing, speaking, open source, or comparable). - Experience with knowledge graphs, vector stores, or other semantic infrastructure for agent context/memory. - Familiarity with eval/validation frameworks for agentic outputs, beyond "vibes." - Curiosity about and exposure to forefront agentic technology in the private or defense sectors, and comfort exploring unproven, emerging tools and approaches. ## Indicators of Success A successful Staff Outcome Designer will, within six months: - Have shipped a working version of the agentic design platform that Product Designers and Design Engineers are actually using. - Have at least one production-support system live (intake/evaluation, release QA, or telemetry) that's measurably reducing manual toil or catching issues before they ship. - Have kicked off or be leading at least one moonshot exploration into forefront agentic customer experiences, with clear cross-functional participation. - Be able to show adoption/impact numbers, not just system architecture diagrams. - title: Creative Lead (Social & UGC)
desc: ## Who we are Creative Milkshake is a remote-first performance creative agency. We make scroll-stopping short-form ads for some of the world's most exciting DTC brands on Meta and TikTok - high-volume, fast-moving, and built to convert. We're a close-knit team of ~34 people spread across the Netherlands, the Philippines, South Africa, Spain, and beyond. We've recently joined the Fieldtrip group alongside inBeat, which means we're growing - in ambition, in capability, and in the complexity of clients we work with. Our Amsterdam studio is the creative heart of our production operation. Over the next 1–2 years, we're expanding from UGC-first content toward elevated branded formats, this role is central to holding the quality bar as we scale. ## The role We make a lot of content. Across a portfolio of DTC clients, our studio shoots and edits dozens of UGC ads every week. Most of it is good. Some of it is great. And the difference between good and great is specific: the hook that actually stops the scroll, the edit that holds attention, the subtle thing that makes a piece of content feel native rather than forced. That's what this role is about. We're looking for a Creative Lead (Social & UGC) to be the final creative eye before work reaches clients. You'll review raw footage, storyboards, and final edits, and give the kind of specific, hands-on feedback that actually improves the work rather than just flags problems. You've made content yourself. You've been on set, you've been in the edit, you know what it takes to make a 15-second video that does something to the person watching it. You bring that maker's instinct to a quality and creative leadership role, and you use it to raise the bar across a whole studio. ## Timezone preference For this role, we're only considering candidates based in +/−3 hrs CET time zone. ## What you'll do ## Hold the creative quality bar - Review storyboards, raw footage when necessary, and final edits before they go to clients - Be the quality gate: if something isn't ready, you say so clearly, and you explain exactly what needs to change and why - Build and maintain the ad example library, creative checklists, and “what good looks like” guides that codify your instinct into something the whole team can learn from - Spot recurring patterns: editing habits that aren't working, storyboard mistakes that keep appearing, hooks that aren't landing. Address them at the root, not ad by ad ## Give hands-on creative direction in post - Review raw footage after shoots and provide clear direction on what's usable, what's not, and what to do differently next time - Give precise editing feedback to our video editors: pacing, cut points, text overlays, sound design, the craft layer that turns a decent edit into something that performs - Understand design fundamentals well enough to give direction on static assets, thumbnail frames, and text treatments: what reads on a phone screen and what doesn't - Know what a 9:16 UGC ad needs to do in the first 2 seconds, and be able to articulate it in a way an editor can act on immediately ## Support production with a creative eye - Review storyboards before shoots and flag what isn't shootable as written, what talent or set requirements are missing, and where the brief and the concept have drifted - Give production the creative context they need to go into a shoot prepared: what angles matter, what the edit is going to need, what “good” looks like for this format and this brand - Periodically join shoots at the Amsterdam studio (+-3 times a year) when creative stakes are high or a new format is being tested - Over time, help build a visual reference library for the studio: what set styles, lighting setups, and shooting approaches produce the most versatile footage ## Drive platform and content intelligence - Maintain a genuine, current relationship with TikTok, Meta, and emerging short-form platforms: scrolling with a critical eye, not just awareness - Curate a regular inspiration feed for the team: specific content examples with notes on why they work, what the craft decisions are, and how we could produce something similar in our studio - Know the difference between a format worth adopting and a trend worth skipping, and be able to make the case either way - Bring fresh creative references when the team's output starts feeling formulaic or dated ## Build the team's creative instinct - Give Creative Strategists feedback on CSPs and scripts that builds their creative eye over time, not just fixes the brief in front of them - Run regular creative review sessions and inspiration shares that create a shared language for what “good” means at Creative Milkshake - Be the person the team brings work to when they're not sure if it's there yet, and give them an answer they can trust ## Own CM's creative identity externally - Approve CM's own social content and website portfolio: what we put out about ourselves should reflect the standard we hold for clients - Help define and document CM's creative POV over time: the format instincts, the aesthetic signatures, the things that make our content recognizably ours ## Who you are We're not filtering on titles. We're looking for a specific type of person: someone with a sharp creative eye for what works on social, who wants to use that experience to raise the quality of an entire studio's output. - 3–7 years of hands-on experience in video production, editing, content creation, or a creative role at a social-first agency or DTC brand. You've made things, not just briefed them - A genuine, current feel for short-form social content: you scroll TikTok and Meta with a critical eye, you notice what's working before it's obvious, and you can describe the craft decisions behind it in specific terms - Ability to understand paid media and performance marketing reports to inform creative decisions - Real editing experience, or close enough collaboration with editors, that you speak the language of the edit - Enough on-set or production experience to spot when a storyboard isn't going to translate, and know what to do about it - The ability to tell a good ad from a great one in seconds, and explain why in a way the person who made it can actually use - Feedback that is specific, timestamped, and producible, not vague creative notes that leave people guessing - High EQ: you can give honest creative feedback without damaging the confidence or the relationship of the person on the other end - Comfortable with ambiguity and pace: we're building systems while operating at volume - Fluent in English, confident presenting creative rationale to clients when needed ## Backgrounds that tend to produce this person There's no single path. People who are great at this role often come from one of these places: - A video editor or post-production lead who has developed a strong creative eye for social, and wants to work upstream on quality rather than just executing edits - A UGC creator or content creator who has built a real, granular understanding of what performs and why, and wants to bring that instinct to a studio environment at scale - A creative producer who sits between strategy and production, has strong taste, and wants to formalise that into a quality leadership role - A social content lead or in-house creative at a DTC brand who has been hands-on with short-form video and wants to take their creative judgement further What they all share: they've made things, they have taste, and they can teach it. ## You'll thrive here if… - You get genuinely excited about the craft of short-form video: the hook, the cut, the text timing, the sound. You find it hard to watch a mediocre ad without knowing what you'd fix - You want a role where your creative instinct directly improves what goes out the door every week - You're energised by the challenge of holding a high standard at volume: lots of content, lots of clients, fast turnarounds - You want to shape creative culture from the inside: setting a standard, building the resources that make a team better, defining what “good” means at a growing studio - The idea of helping a UGC studio move toward elevated social-first content over the next couple of years sounds like exactly the right moment to join ## This role isn't for you if… - You've only worked in creative strategy or performance marketing and haven't been hands-on with video production or editing - Your creative background is in brand identity or traditional advertising rather than short-form, social-first content - You prefer to stay in the strategic or conceptual space and find production and editing detail less interesting - You're primarily looking for a people-management role. Your influence here comes through creative expertise, not team size ## What we offer - Creative Milkshake Stipends (mental health, healthcare & internet) - Time Off: 21 days PTO + 7 Paid Sick Days; company closure: 2 weeks at year-end (estimated: December 22 – January 5) - Maternity/Paternity Leave - Yearly Salary Review - Long Service Incentives (starting from 2 years)

Build and lead a team of 2–3 Operations Managers embedded across those delivery functions - Design and implement scalable workflows, documentation, and tooling that grow with the team. - Own and standardize inBeat's operational tech stack (Airtable, ClickUp, Notion, Make/N8N/Zapier, Claude, Fathom, G-Suite), making clear what tools we use, how we use them, and where - Deep understanding of how creative delivery functions work - UGC, video, design, paid media, influencer - not just one or two of them - Track record of building systems and processes that teams actually use and love. - High fluency across project management and ops tooling - Airtable, ClickUp, Notion, Make/Zapier/N8N or equivalents - Systems thinker who can see the full operational picture and translate it into clear, well-documented processes - Strong communicator who can build trust and buy-in with department leads across different creative disciplines - Comfortable operating in high-growth, ambiguous environments - you can build structure without needing everything figured out first ## While not required, it's an added plus if you also have - Experience with backend finance ops, HR ops, or IT ops at an agency - Familiarity with AI-assisted operations tooling - Experience scaling an agency through the 100 to 200+ headcount range - Background in performance marketing, influencer marketing, or paid media operations ## Why join us? - Low bureaucracy. High ownership. You will not be waiting for permission to fix things - Fully remote (with the possibility to work from anywhere) - Flexible hours - Unlimited Time Off & Sick Days - Five fast-growing companies under one portfolio - 200+ team members globally - Work directly with the COO & Chief Creative Officer - High-paced, entrepreneurial environment - Most systems are being rebuilt - this is a hands-on role where your work becomes the new standard

title: Head Of Organic Social
desc: ## About us inBeat is a creative growth agency, now part of the Fieldtrip group. We make creator content at serious volume for brands like Bumble, Miro, Hurom, and NielsenIQ, and we tie every piece of it back to performance data. Small autonomous teams, fast pace, no layers of approval between you and the work. ## Why this role exists This is a full-time, fully remote position that allows work from anywhere/everywhere in the world. Organic social keeps landing on our plate. Clients hire us for UGC and paid, then ask us to run their organic channels too. Without really trying, it's grown into a business line closing in on seven figures. No dedicated lead, no playbook, no team behind it yet. That's the job. You'd be employee one of this department. Nothing to inherit. You build the offer, the processes, the team, and the client results that let us scale it. ## What you'll do - Run our current organic accounts yourself for the first few months. Strategy, content direction, posting cadence, reporting. You build the department by doing the work first. - Design how we deliver: recurring creator pods, weekly posting systems, repurposing our UGC and paid assets for organic. Systems that put out volume every week without heroics. - Package the offer. Scopes, rate cards, and audits we can sell more than once. - Hire strategists, producers, and editors as the book grows, and lead them well. - Own the numbers. Report on organic the way a performance marketer would: growth, engagement, and what it feeds into paid. Our clients are performance people and they can smell a vanity metric a mile away. - Work with sales and account teams on pitches, audits, and upsells. Organic is our fastest growing expansion motion with existing clients, so you'll be in the room a lot. ## Who you are - Think internal social team: marketers who make their own content. You know hooks, formats, angles, and edit pacing, and you can read a dashboard and change course when the data tells you to. - You live on these platforms. You know which trends, sounds, and formats are peaking and which are already dead, and you can turn a cultural moment into brand-appropriate content in days. Reactive, culture-led content is a big part of how we win. - You've run organic social with your own hands, at a lean in-house team or an agency, and grown accounts yourself rather than managed people who did. - Lead level, not big-company senior. We don't care if you've never run a 20 person team. We care that you've set creative direction, shipped daily, and want to build a department around what works. - Comfortable with creators: briefing them, directing them, and building repeatable systems around UGC talent. - Fine with ambiguity. There's no machine to operate here yet. You're building it. - Bonus points if you have agency experience across several brands at once, or enough paid social fluency to make organic and paid feed each other. ## This role is not for you if - You want to set strategy and hand off execution from day one. - Your background is brand identity and polished campaigns rather than social-first content. - You need a finished playbook to operate. The offer and packages exist. - 6 months: first hires made. New organic retainers signed with existing clients. One reporting standard across accounts. - 12 months: a profitable organic social department with its own playbook, team, and pipeline. ## Why join us? - Unlimited Time Off & Sick Days - Flexible hours - Fully remote (with the possibility to work from anywhere) - Reports to inBeat leadership. - We want this filled fast. It's a priority search, so if this sounds like you, apply and we will move quickly.
